description: Phase 2 retrieval tuning corpus. Each seed atom is hand-crafted so the queries below have a deterministic expected top-1. If retrieval changes (new ranker, new embedding model, new tuning constants), running this corpus tells you immediately whether quality moved forward or backward.

atoms.body: Reece asked about ballpark cost in the first five minutes, before we discussed deliverables. Anchor risk: budget number sets mental ceiling regardless of value framing.
Reece will send the three best manually-written ads from this quarter by Friday so we can reverse-engineer the winning rubric.
Reece has around 1000 notes in an Obsidian vault. The ad-bot drafts copy by pulling from those notes via retrieval.
The ad-bot grabs wrong source notes — pulls a six-month-old note when a fresher one exists. No tagging system; the vault is organized by timestamp and title only.
Reece hasn't defined what a 'winning ad' looks like. He knows the manually-written ones convert 2.3x better but can't articulate the criteria. We're tuning blind until we name the rubric.
Reece deflected the question about who on his team would own the ad-bot tooling day to day. Suggests team adoption risk that hasn't been addressed.
When the 10-day pilot at $12k fixed was floated, Reece said 'that's actually really fair' — strong buying signal on the pilot frame.

queries.name: price_question
queries.window: what does this cost like ballpark for a full engagement
queries.rationale: Window mentions cost + ballpark; the price-anchor atom uses the exact same words.

queries.name: retrieval_complaint
queries.window: the agent keeps grabbing the wrong notes from the vault, pulling old stuff instead of recent
queries.rationale: Direct semantic match on retrieval problems with wrong notes.

queries.name: next_step_commitment
queries.window: okay so what are you going to send me by end of week
queries.rationale: Window about deliverables by week-end matches the Friday commitment.

queries.name: definition_of_done
queries.window: before we build anything we need to define what a good ad even looks like
queries.rationale: Defining winning criteria — semantic match on the framing insight.

queries.name: stack_check
queries.window: where do you store your notes and how big is your knowledge base
queries.rationale: Stack/storage question maps to the vault-size fact.
